processing_steps.method: vacuum induction melting and casting into cylindrical copper moulds
processing_steps.cooling_medium: cylindrical copper moulds (32 mm in diameter by 186 mm in length)
processing_steps.processing_steps_notes: No further heat treatment reported; terminal state is as-cast.

processing_steps.method: cut from cast ingots by spark erosion; specimen surfaces ground
processing_steps.processing_steps_notes: Specimens cut in the direction of the longitudinal axis of the ingot (casting direction); compression specimens (6×6×10) mm³; tensile specimens (3.5×5) mm² cross-section with 15 mm gauge length.

structures.overall_structure: Three-phase: Fe3Al matrix + NbC carbides + Laves phase (Fe,Al)2Nb

defect_interactions.qualitative_or_quantitative_description: Different elastic properties of matrix and secondary phases result in internal tensions during solidification; precipitates act as notches, contributing to tension-compression asymmetry.

interfaces.phase_evolution: Laves phase (Fe,Al)₂Nb provides efficient strengthening; MC carbides show higher temperature stability and higher resistance to coarsening than the Laves phase.

measurement_conditions.specimen_geometry: compression specimens (6×6×10) mm³; tensile specimens (3.5×5) mm² cross-section with 15 mm gauge length
measurement_conditions.other_conditions: samples cut along longitudinal ingot axis (casting direction); specimen surfaces ground; ZWICK 1474 universal testing machine

tensile_properties.stress_strain_curves: Room-temperature compression curve (curve 11 in Fig. 2b) hardens with nearly constant slope over long strain intervals, approaching the 2000 MPa gridline; room-temperature tension curve (curve 11 in Fig. 3b) peaks between the 500 and 600 MPa gridlines.

measurement_conditions.other_conditions: held 30 min at testing temperature before loading; temperature checked by NiCr-Ni thermocouple on specimen surface

tensile_properties.stress_strain_curves: Fe-26Al-4Nb-1C is the highest curve over the whole temperature range, starting near the 800 MPa gridline and peaking just above the 600 MPa gridline at about 500 °C.

measurement_conditions.other_conditions: held 30 min at testing temperature before loading

lower than compression (graphical reading; no numeric labels printed)

measurement_conditions.other_conditions: held 30 min at testing temperature before loading

comparative_performance.comparison_metric: yield stress in compression (room temperature and elevated temperature)

characterization_methods.instrument_or_setup: load 62.5 g; indentation ball 2.5 mm diameter
ZWICK 1474 universal testing machine; deformation rate 10^-4 s^-1; radiation furnace for elevated-temperature tests
characterization_methods.measurement_conditions: room temperature and 650/800 °C in protective argon; specimens held 30 min at testing temperature before loading
characterization_methods.purpose: determine yield stress, ductility, hardening and tension-compression asymmetry
characterization_methods.key_findings: RT compression yield stress 792 MPa; yield stress anomaly peak 474 °C / 619 MPa; tension-compression asymmetry at RT and elevated temperatures

characterization_methods.instrument_or_setup: SEM-Hitachi S-530; 20 kV; working distance 15 mm; secondary electrons (SE)
characterization_methods.measurement_conditions: fracture surfaces of tensile specimens after room-temperature testing
characterization_methods.key_findings: intergranular decohesion besides transgranular cleavage (IGD+TGC); rough intergranular decohesion areas with densely distributed precipitates (Fig. 4k)

unmapped_findings: [b0033] Room-temperature tensile yield stress and total elongation are reported as '-' (not determined/not reported) in Table 2 for Fe-26Al-4Nb-1C; mode of fracture is IGD+TGC (intergranular decohesion + transgranular cleavage).

[b0035] Fe-26Al-4Nb-1C shows totally brittle behaviour at room temperature (together with Fe-26Al-4Ti-1C); its intergranular fracture areas contain many densely distributed precipitates that make the decohesion areas rough rather than smooth.
[b0024] Fe-26Al-4Nb-1C is the only Fe-26Al-based alloy that does not exhibit lower yield stress in compression than the binary Fe-26Al alloy at room temperature.

[b0038] Fe-26Al-4Nb-1C exhibits the most significant shift of the yield stress anomaly peak (474 °C, 619 MPa) among the Fe-26Al-based alloys, demonstrating the strengthening effect of the Laves phase (Fe,Al)2Nb; MC carbides have higher temperature stability and resistance to coarsening than the Laves phase.
[figure_006] In Fig. 6b, Fe-26Al-4Nb-1C lies highest at every tested temperature and its yield-stress anomaly peak is displaced to lower temperature and higher stress relative to binary Fe-26Al.
